1. The petitioner filed this petition under Section 166 of Motor Vehicles Act 1989, seeking compensation of Rs.15,00,000/- for the injures sustained by him in the road traffic accident occurred on 22.05.2023.
2.

It is the case of the petitioner that, on 22.05.2023 at about 2-40 p.m., within the jurisdiction of V.V.Puram Traffic Police Station, Mysore, behind Samasth Hotel northern side of high tension double road, Vijayanagara 2nd Stage, when the Petitioner was riding unoffending Yamaha Crucz Motor Cycle bearing Reg. No.KA-09-HB- 3465 and while taking right turn by giving indications to following vehicles at that time accused No.1 being a driver of the offending Maruthi 800 car bearing Reg.
M.V.C.No.4154/2023 3 SCCH - 7 No.KA-09-N-1348 drove the same towards Vijayanagara Water Tank in a high speed, rash and negligent manner so as to endangering human life and dashed against the left side of the unoffending vehicle, as a result the Petitioner fall on the road and sustained grievous injuries.

Further it is alleged that at the time of accident the accused No.1 has not possessing valid and effective driving licence to drive the offending vehicle and the RC owner/
Accused No.2 of the offending vehicle has permitted the accused No.1 to drive the offending vehicle.

Thereafter Petitioner was shifted to Supriya Hospital, Mysore wherein he was treated as an inpatient and undergone surgery and he has spent Rs.1,00,000/- towards medical expenditure and other incidental charges.
In this regard the Informant /Siddegowda. H has lodged complaint before the V.V. Puram Traffic police station, Mysore.

. Further it is contended that, prior to the alleged accident the Petitioner was hale, healthy and he was aged about 43 years and he was working as Process Server, Judicial Department and getting salary of Rs.41,789/- p.m.
Due to the injuries sustained in the alleged accident he lost his income and future prospective life, happiness, and earning capacity and become disabled and dependent.
The alleged accident is occurred due to fault and negligence act of the driver of the offending offending Maruthi 800 car bearing Reg. No.KA-09-N-1348.
Respondent No.1 is the RC owner and Respondent No.2 is the Insurer of the said offending vehicle, as such the respondents are jointly and severally liable to pay compensation to Petitioner.
Hence Petitioner filed the present claim petition for seeking compensation.

:: I S S U E S ::
(1) Whether the Petitioner proves that the accident occurred due to rash and negligent act of driving of Car bearing Reg. No.KA-09-N-1348 and as a result, he sustained injuries?
(2) Whether the Petitioner proves the age and earnings of the Petitioner as stated in the claim petition?
(3) Whether the petitioner is entitled for compensation?
If so, how much and from whom?

(4) What order or award?

sentences.text: It is not in dispute as to the aspect that, the Petitioner sustained grievous injuries in the alleged incident.

Because, for the above reasons collectively it is clear that,
the accident happened due to rash and negligent act of the accused.

At the same time, it has come out in evidence that the alleged accident was occurred due to rash and negligent driving of the offending vehicle and fault of the accused.

Matters being so, the acts of the accused person clearly constitute the offences punishable under sections 279 & 338 of IPC R/w Section 3(1) R/w 181, 5(1)

Thus because of such negligent act of the accused No.1/driver of the offending vehicle, it resulted in the injuries of the innocent man/Petitioner aforesaid, as he/accused No.1 drove the said offending vehicle very rashly or negligently on the spot.
Therefore, the alleged accident occurred due to the fault of the accused M.V.C.No.4154/2023 19 SCCH - 7 No.1/driver of the offending vehicle.

Oriental Insurance Company Ltd., and others and the Hon'ble Court held that the award passed against insured owner to be paid by the insurer and recovered from owner.

opennyai_summary.ANALYSIS:
The alleged accident was occurred due to rash and negligent driving of the offending vehicle and fault of the accused.
Therefore, considering the above discussed aspects collectively, it is the considered opinion of the Court that, the incident having been taken place in the manner asserted by the prosecution and the same being proved to have been taken place in the manner alleged by the prosecution, the accused No.1 drew the offending vehicle in a rash or negligent manner so as to endanger human life and at the spot dashed to the unoffending vehicle, as a result Petitioner sustained grievous M.V.C.No.4154/2023 18 SCCH - 7 injuries.
It is evident that injuries noted in the Ex.P6/Wound Certificate would be caused by a road accident.
At the same time, it has come out in evidence that the alleged accident was occurred due to rash and negligent driving of the offending vehicle and fault of the accused.
Matters being so, the acts of the accused person clearly constitute the offences punishable under sections 279 & 338 of IPC R/w Section 3(1) R/w 181, 5(1)
R/w Sec. 180 of MV Act.
Thus because of such negligent act of the accused No.1/driver of the offending vehicle, it resulted in the injuries of the innocent man/Petitioner aforesaid, as he/accused No.1 drove the said offending vehicle very rashly or negligently on the spot.
Therefore, the alleged accident occurred due to the fault of the accused M.V.C.No.4154/2023 19 SCCH - 7 No.1/driver of the offending vehicle.
In the instance case the petitioner claimed that he was working as a Process Server in Judicial Department and getting salary of Rs.41,789/-.
Therefore the petitioner is not entitled for compensation under the head of loss of future earnings and loss of income during laid up period.
The principle of pay and recovery is explained in detail in the decision reported in (2018) 3 SCC 208 in the case of Pappu and Others V/s Vinod Kumar Lamba and Another and (2018) 9 SCC 650 in the case of Shamanna and another V/s Divisional Manager,
Oriental Insurance Company Ltd., and others and the Hon'ble Court held that the award passed against insured owner to be paid by the insurer and recovered from owner.
In view of the Ex.P-7/ Charge Sheet, evidence and material available on record it is seen that the driver of the offending vehicle is not possessing valid and effected licence at the time of M.V.C.No.4154/2023 26 SCCH - 7 alleged accident and accordingly the case is rightly registered against the accused No.1/driver of the offending vehicle under Section 279 & 338 of IPC R/w Section 3(1) R/w 181, 5(1) R/w Sec. 180 of MV Act.
In the instance case it is admitted fact that the driver/ Respondent No.1/RC owner of the offending vehicle has not possessed valid driving licence at the time of the alleged accident and therefore there is clear violation of the terms and conditions of the insurance policy, as such in view of breach of the policy condition the Petitioner prays to direct the Insurance Company to pay the compensation and recovered from the owner/ Respondent No.1 of the offending vehicle.
The Court, therefore, holds that mere omission of proviso attached to sub-section (4) of Section 149 of Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 after its replacement by Section 150 of Motor Vehicles (Amendment) Act, 2019 (32 of 2019), neither takes away the liability of the insurer to pay the claimants nor its right to recover the said amount from the owner.
The law to this effect remains intact and unaffected by Amendment Act, 2019 and, hence, insurer shall continue to indemnify the owner's risk in relation to accidents taking place after 01.04.2022 and "PAY & RECOVER" principle will still continue to govern the field advancing social object of the Statute protecting third party interest.
Principle of law laid down by the Supreme Court in National Insurance Company Limited vs. Swaran Singh and others, JT 2004 (1) SC 109 has not lost its significance and binding effect despite omission of proviso.
